entries.vi: liên hệ lại, theo sát tiếp
entries.en: To contact someone again to continue or check on a previous discussion.
ex: I'll follow up with the client tomorrow about the proposal.
Just following up on my last email — any updates?

entries.vi: làm rõ phạm vi công việc
entries.en: To make the boundaries and deliverables of a project clear before starting.
ex: Can we clarify scope before we quote the price?
Let's clarify the scope so we don't do unpaid extra work.

entries.vi: thống nhất kỳ vọng hai bên
entries.en: To make sure everyone agrees on goals, timing and quality before starting.
ex: Let's align expectations on the timeline before kickoff.
We lost the client because we never aligned expectations.

entries.vi: đầu việc cần làm (sau cuộc họp)
entries.en: A specific task assigned to someone as a result of a meeting.
ex: Thanks, I'll turn that feedback into an action item.
Every meeting should end with clear action items and owners.

entries.vi: người có quyền quyết định
entries.en: The person who has the authority to approve or reject a deal or plan.
ex: Before the demo, let's confirm who the decision maker is.
I'd love to include the decision maker in our next call.

entries.vi: vấn đề nhức nhối của khách hàng
entries.en: A specific problem that frustrates a customer and that your product can solve.
ex: Manual reporting is their biggest pain point.
Start the pitch from the customer's pain point, not the features.

entries.vi: giá trị cốt lõi mang lại cho khách
entries.en: A clear statement of the benefit a customer gets from your product or service.
ex: Our value proposition is saving teams ten hours a week.
If the value proposition isn't clear in one sentence, rewrite it.

entries.vi: bản chứng minh ý tưởng khả thi
entries.en: A small demo built to show that an idea can actually work.
ex: We shipped a proof of concept in two weeks to win the deal.
Let's run a proof of concept before committing the full budget.

entries.vi: kế hoạch triển khai theo giai đoạn
entries.en: A step-by-step plan for releasing a product or change to users.
ex: The rollout plan starts with a pilot group of ten users.
A phased rollout plan reduces the risk of big failures.

entries.vi: kiểm định chất lượng (QA)
entries.en: The process of checking work meets standards before delivery.
ex: Quality assurance caught the bug before the client ever saw it.
Budget one day of quality assurance for every release.

entries.vi: giữ liên lạc
entries.en: To continue communicating with someone after meeting them.
ex: It was great seeing you — let's keep in touch.
We kept in touch after the conference and later became partners.

entries.vi: phá băng, mở đầu cho đỡ ngại
entries.en: To say or do something that makes people feel relaxed at the start.
ex: A light question about travel helped break the ice.
He told a short story to break the ice before the pitch.

entries.vi: áp lực chạy hạn chót
entries.en: Stress caused by having limited time to finish work.
ex: The team performs well even under deadline pressure.
Deadline pressure is no excuse for skipping QA.

entries.vi: yêu cầu của khách hàng
entries.en: Something the client explicitly needs the product or service to do.
ex: Write down every client requirement before estimating.
This feature isn't a client requirement — park it for later.

entries.vi: tiếp nhận và xử lý góp ý
entries.en: To respond to criticism calmly and turn it into improvements.
ex: She handles feedback well and never takes it personally.
Handling feedback gracefully is a leadership skill.

entries.vi: có tiến triển
entries.en: To move forward toward finishing a goal.
ex: We're making steady progress on the migration.
Small daily wins are how you make real progress.

entries.vi: ranh giới cá nhân
entries.en: A limit someone sets to protect their time, privacy, energy, or comfort.
ex: He explained his personal boundary politely and clearly.
Setting personal boundaries prevents burnout.

entries.vi: khiếu hài hước
entries.en: The ability to see and share what is funny in situations.
ex: A good sense of humor makes meetings feel lighter.
Clients remember people with a warm sense of humor.

entries.vi: ấn tượng ban đầu
entries.en: The opinion someone forms when they first meet a person or see a product.
ex: The homepage creates the first impression of the product.
You never get a second chance to make a first impression.

entries.vi: đi chơi, tụ tập thư giãn
entries.en: To spend relaxed, informal time with people.
ex: We should hang out after the conference some time.
The team hangs out every Friday evening.

entries.vi: hàn huyên cập nhật tin tức; đuổi kịp việc
entries.en: To talk with someone you haven't seen for a while, or to reach the required level of work.
ex: Let's catch up over coffee next week.
I need the weekend to catch up on emails.

entries.vi: ranh giới, giới hạn
entries.en: A line that marks a limit — physical, personal, or professional.
ex: Clear boundaries between work and life keep you healthy.
The contract sets the boundary of our responsibilities.

entries.vi: một cách lịch sự
entries.en: In a way that shows good manners and respect.
ex: She politely declined the meeting invite.
Disagree politely: say 'I see it differently' instead of 'you're wrong'.

entries.vi: một cách vô tình, không cố ý
entries.en: By chance, without intending to.
ex: I accidentally sent the draft to the whole team.
He accidentally deleted the file, but we had a backup.

entries.vi: ngượng ngùng nhưng chân thành
entries.en: Uncomfortable to say, yet truthful and sincere.
ex: His awkward but honest apology won the client back.
An awkward but honest answer beats a smooth lie.

entries.vi: cuộc họp hỗn loạn, không kiểm soát
entries.en: A meeting with no structure where everyone talks over each other.
ex: An agenda is the cure for a chaotic meeting.
The launch review turned into a chaotic meeting with no decisions.

entries.vi: vô tình trông chuyên nghiệp
entries.en: Looking professional without planning to — usually a happy surprise.
ex: The quick demo looked accidentally professional, so the client asked for a pilot.
My messy notes turned into an accidentally professional proposal.

entries.vi: đơ não, quên sạch trong giây lát
entries.en: A sudden moment when you cannot think or remember anything.
ex: I had a brain freeze in the interview when they asked my salary expectation.
Take a breath if you get brain freeze during a presentation.

entries.vi: cú ngoặt bất ngờ
entries.en: An unexpected change in a story or situation.
ex: Plot twist: the intern's idea won the pitch.
The acquisition was a plot twist nobody saw coming.

entries.vi: vấn đề gây tranh cãi
entries.en: A topic that people strongly disagree about.
ex: Pricing changes are a controversial issue inside the team.
Handle controversial issues with data, not opinions.

entries.vi: hệ quả dài hạn
entries.en: A result that appears long after the decision that caused it.
ex: Technical debt is the long-term consequence of rushed code.
Consider the long-term consequences before cutting the QA budget.

entries.vi: ý nghĩa thực tiễn, tác động thực tế
entries.en: What an idea or decision actually means for day-to-day work.
ex: The practical implication of the new policy is two extra approvals per order.
Explain the practical implications, not just the theory.

entries.vi: yếu tố quan trọng, then chốt
entries.en: Something that strongly influences a result.
ex: Response time is a significant factor in customer satisfaction.
Price was a significant factor, but trust closed the deal.

entries.vi: lập luận mạch lạc
entries.en: A line of reasoning where every point connects logically.
ex: The essay needs a coherent argument, not a list of random opinions.
She made a coherent argument for doubling the content budget.

entries.vi: đánh giá bằng chứng, số liệu
entries.en: To examine facts carefully before drawing a conclusion.
ex: Evaluate the evidence before blaming the new release.
Good managers evaluate evidence instead of trusting the loudest voice.

entries.vi: kết luận cân bằng, khách quan
entries.en: A final judgment that fairly considers both sides.
ex: The report ends with a balanced conclusion on both vendors.
A balanced conclusion mentions risks, not only benefits.

entries.vi: trao đổi nhanh, cập nhật ngắn
entries.en: To have a brief conversation to stay updated.
ex: Let's touch base on Friday to review progress.
I just wanted to touch base before the client call.

entries.vi: quay lại bàn sau
entries.en: To return to a topic later after more thought or information.
ex: Good question — let me circle back after I check the numbers.
We'll circle back to pricing once the demo is done.

entries.vi: nhận trách nhiệm trọn vẹn về việc
entries.en: To treat a task as fully your responsibility, including its results.
ex: She took ownership of the bug and fixed the process behind it.
Take ownership — don't wait to be told what to do.

entries.vi: hiểu và thống nhất với nhau
entries.en: Having the same understanding about a plan or situation.
ex: Before we start, let's make sure we're on the same page about scope.
A short recap email keeps everyone on the same page.

entries.vi: tạo thay đổi đáng kể
entries.en: To make a noticeable difference in results.
ex: Small tweaks won't move the needle — we need a new channel.
This partnership could really move the needle on revenue.

entries.vi: việc dễ làm mà hiệu quả ngay
entries.en: The easiest wins that give quick results with little effort.
ex: Fixing the checkout button is low-hanging fruit — do it first.
We picked the low-hanging fruit; now the hard work begins.

entries.vi: sản phẩm bàn giao
entries.en: A concrete piece of work you must hand over to the client.
ex: The deliverables are a logo pack and a brand guideline PDF.
List every deliverable in the contract to avoid disputes.

entries.vi: mốc quan trọng của dự án
entries.en: A key checkpoint that marks real progress in a project.
ex: The first milestone is a working demo by March.
We celebrate every milestone to keep the team motivated.

entries.vi: nút thắt cổ chai làm chậm cả hệ
entries.en: The single point that slows down the whole process.
ex: Design review is the bottleneck — everything waits for it.
Remove the bottleneck instead of pushing people to work faster.

entries.vi: sự đánh đổi
entries.en: Accepting a downside to gain a more important upside.
ex: Speed versus quality is the classic trade-off.
Every architecture decision is a trade-off — name it clearly.

entries.vi: đôi bên cùng có lợi
entries.en: An outcome where both sides benefit.
ex: A longer contract at a lower monthly price is a win-win.
Aim for win-win deals — they create repeat customers.

entries.vi: con số ước lượng sơ bộ
entries.en: A rough estimate, not an exact number.
ex: Can you give me a ballpark figure for the whole project?
As a ballpark figure, expect around ten thousand dollars.

entries.vi: chốt đơn, chốt hợp đồng
entries.en: To get the final agreement and signature from a customer.
ex: A live demo is what finally closed the deal.
Follow up fast — slow replies lose deals, quick ones close them.

entries.vi: xử lý lời từ chối của khách
entries.en: Responding to a customer's doubts so the sale can continue.
ex: Good objection handling starts with listening, not arguing.
Prepare objection handling for price, timing, and trust.

entries.vi: bán thêm gói cao hơn
entries.en: To offer a customer a bigger or better version of what they buy.
ex: We upsell the premium support plan at checkout.
Don't upsell before the customer trusts the basic product.

entries.vi: tỉ lệ khách rời bỏ
entries.en: The rate at which customers stop using your product.
ex: Churn dropped after we improved onboarding.
High churn means the product promise isn't being kept.

entries.vi: quy trình làm quen cho người mới
entries.en: The process of helping a new user or employee get started successfully.
ex: Great onboarding cuts support tickets in half.
Her onboarding buddy answered questions all week.

entries.vi: bên liên quan
entries.en: Anyone affected by or interested in a project's outcome.
ex: Invite every stakeholder to the kickoff meeting.
Keep stakeholders updated so there are no surprises.

entries.vi: sự đồng thuận, ủng hộ
entries.en: Agreement and support from the people you need.
ex: Get the team's buy-in before changing the process.
Without leadership buy-in, the initiative will stall.

entries.vi: phản biện, từ chối khéo
entries.en: To disagree with or resist a request professionally.
ex: It's okay to push back on an unrealistic deadline.
She pushed back politely with data to support her case.

entries.vi: góp ý mang tính xây dựng
entries.en: Criticism given to help someone improve, not to blame.
ex: Constructive feedback focuses on the work, not the person.
Ask for constructive feedback after every big delivery.

entries.vi: họp rút kinh nghiệm sau sự kiện
entries.en: A short meeting after an event to review what happened and learn.
ex: Let's debrief right after the client presentation.
The debrief revealed why the launch was delayed.

entries.vi: làm tới nơi tới chốn điều đã hứa
entries.en: To actually complete what you promised to do.
ex: He always follows through, so clients trust him.
Ideas are cheap; following through is what builds reputation.

entries.vi: báo trước cho biết
entries.en: An early warning or notice about something coming.
ex: Just a heads-up: the server maintenance is tonight.
Thanks for the heads-up about the price change.

entries.vi: đưa ai đó vào luồng trao đổi
entries.en: To include someone in a conversation or email thread.
ex: Looping in our designer so she has full context.
Please loop me in on any client escalations.

entries.vi: như email trước đã nói (nhắc khéo)
entries.en: A polite-but-firm way to point back to information already sent.
ex: Per my last email, the invoice was due on Friday.
Use 'per my last email' carefully — it can sound passive-aggressive.

entries.vi: từ nay về sau
entries.en: From now on; starting from this point.
ex: Moving forward, all requests go through the ticket system.
Let's agree on one communication channel moving forward.

entries.vi: chủ động liên hệ
entries.en: To contact someone, especially to offer or ask for help.
ex: Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.
I reached out to three suppliers for quotes.

entries.vi: đính kèm là... (văn phong email)
entries.en: A formal email phrase meaning the document is attached.
ex: Attached please find the signed contract.
Attached please find the Q3 report for your review.

entries.vi: chinh phục cả khán phòng
entries.en: To gain the attention and support of everyone in a presentation.
ex: She won the room with one honest customer story.
Numbers inform, but stories win the room.

entries.vi: bài giới thiệu 30 giây
entries.en: A very short, clear summary of your idea that fits an elevator ride.
ex: Practice your elevator pitch until it's under thirty seconds.
His elevator pitch got us the second meeting.

entries.vi: điều quan trọng nhất cần nhớ
entries.en: The most important point people should remember.
ex: The key takeaway: retention matters more than downloads.
End every slide deck with three key takeaways.

entries.vi: trình bày từng bước
entries.en: To explain something step by step.
ex: Let me walk you through the new dashboard.
She walked the client through the onboarding flow.

entries.vi: kết thúc, chốt lại
entries.en: To finish or conclude something.
ex: Let's wrap up with action items and owners.
We wrapped up the project two days early.

entries.vi: mức lương mong muốn
entries.en: The pay you hope to receive for a job.
ex: When asked about salary expectations, give a researched range.
My salary expectation is based on market data for this role.

entries.vi: thành tích đã được chứng minh
entries.en: Your history of results that proves what you can do.
ex: Her track record of shipped products speaks for itself.
Show a track record, not just promises, in the interview.

entries.vi: kỹ năng dùng được ở nhiều nghề
entries.en: Abilities useful across different jobs, like communication or planning.
ex: Sales taught me transferable skills like listening and negotiation.
Highlight transferable skills when changing industries.

entries.vi: chủ động làm không cần ai nhắc
entries.en: To act and start things without being told.
ex: She took initiative and automated the weekly report.
Employers love people who take initiative.

entries.vi: làm việc dưới áp lực
entries.en: To stay effective when stressed by deadlines or stakes.
ex: Give one real example of working under pressure in interviews.
The launch proved the team can work under pressure.

entries.vi: thời gian báo trước khi nghỉ việc
entries.en: The time between resigning and actually leaving a job.
ex: My notice period is thirty days.
She used her notice period to hand over cleanly.

entries.vi: đáng đồng tiền, hiệu quả so với chi phí
entries.en: Giving good value for the money spent.
ex: Email marketing is still the most cost-effective channel.
Find a cost-effective way to test the idea first.

entries.vi: dòng doanh thu
entries.en: One distinct source of income for a business.
ex: Ads are our second revenue stream after subscriptions.
Never depend on a single revenue stream.

entries.vi: biên lợi nhuận
entries.en: The percentage of revenue left after costs.
ex: Custom work has a higher profit margin than resale.
Discounts eat straight into the profit margin.

entries.vi: mở rộng quy mô
entries.en: To grow a system or business to handle much more.
ex: We'll scale up ads once the funnel converts.
The server scales up automatically at peak hours.

entries.vi: dồn lực mạnh hơn vào cái đang hiệu quả
entries.en: To commit even more to something that is working.
ex: Shorts are working — let's double down on them.
Double down on winners, cut the losers fast.

entries.vi: chuyển hướng chiến lược
entries.en: To change direction when the current plan isn't working.
ex: We pivoted from an app to a service and revenue tripled.
Knowing when to pivot is as important as persistence.

entries.vi: thẩm định kỹ trước khi quyết định
entries.en: Careful checking done before a big decision or deal.
ex: Do due diligence before signing any partnership.
Their due diligence found risks we had missed.

entries.vi: tóm gọn lại là
entries.en: Summarized in the fewest possible words.
ex: In a nutshell, we grew revenue but lost margin.
Give it to me in a nutshell — one sentence.

entries.vi: điều đáng suy ngẫm
entries.en: An idea worth thinking about carefully.
ex: Your point about pricing is real food for thought.
The customer interview gave us plenty of food for thought.

entries.vi: điểm chung để bắt đầu thỏa thuận
entries.en: Shared interests or opinions that both sides agree on.
ex: Start the negotiation by finding common ground.
We found common ground on quality, then discussed price.

entries.term: put it on the back burner
entries.vi: tạm gác lại, để tính sau
entries.en: To delay something less urgent for later.
ex: Let's put the redesign on the back burner until Q4.
Good ideas go on the back burner, bad ones go in the bin.

entries.vi: khởi động, bắt đầu cho chạy
entries.en: To start something moving.
ex: Let's get the ball rolling with a quick kickoff call.
A small deposit gets the ball rolling on the project.

entries.vi: nghĩ sáng tạo, khác lối mòn
entries.en: To find creative solutions beyond the usual approach.
ex: The zero-budget campaign forced us to think outside the box.
Think outside the box: what if onboarding took one minute?

entries.vi: đi thẳng vào vấn đề
entries.en: To skip small talk and get to the main point.
ex: Let's cut to the chase: can you deliver by Friday?
He cut to the chase and asked about the budget.

entries.vi: hiểu ý ẩn sau lời nói
entries.en: To understand what is meant but not said directly.
ex: Reading between the lines, the client wants a discount.
Her short reply said a lot if you read between the lines.

entries.term: give the benefit of the doubt
entries.vi: tạm tin, không vội nghi ngờ
entries.en: To choose to trust someone even without proof.
ex: He missed the call — give him the benefit of the doubt.
New teammates deserve the benefit of the doubt at first.

entries.vi: hơi mệt trong người
entries.en: Feeling slightly sick.
ex: I'm a bit under the weather, so I'll work from home today.
She sounded under the weather on the call.

entries.vi: ngàn cân treo sợi tóc, chưa chắc chắn
entries.en: Risky and uncertain — the result could go either way.
ex: The deadline was touch and go until the final hour.
Cash flow was touch and go in the first year.
